headline: San Francisco enterprises are hiring builders who can ship agentic AI systems — your move is to design and ship one in the next 90 days.
why_now: With GitHub and project_potential scores above 94 and job_demand at 85 in the SF enterprise market, agentic workflows have moved from research demos to production priorities. Local relevance at 82 confirms Bay Area companies are actively translating multi-step AI agents into customer-facing products. Sitting this out means watching peers capture the most visible AI engineering roles of the cycle.
study: Read Anthropic's 'Building Effective Agents' and the LangChain ReAct paper to internalize planning, tool-use, and reflection patterns.
Complete the LangGraph or CrewAI quickstart and rebuild the example agent from scratch without copy-pasting, then add error handling.
Study MCP (Model Context Protocol) and OpenAI function-calling/tool-use specs; build a small agent that calls at least three real tools (search, SQL, email).
Spend two evenings on evaluation: implement a simple eval harness using Braintrust or plain pytest to grade agent traces and outputs.
Review 3-5 production agent architectures on GitHub (e.g., LangChain templates, AutoGen samples) and write notes on trade-offs.

build.title: Enterprise Sales-Research Agent Swarm
build.description: A multi-agent system where a Planner agent decomposes a target-account brief, a Researcher agent pulls web/news/SEC filings, an Analyst agent scores fit against your ICP, and a Writer agent produces a one-page memo — all coordinated through a shared scratchpad and evaluated end-to-end. This impresses because it mirrors the exact agentic architecture SF enterprise teams (Glean, Harvey, Decagon) are hiring to build.
deliverables: Public GitHub repo with clean README, architecture diagram, and reproducible setup
Live demo deployed on Vercel or Railway with a 90-second Loom walkthrough
Technical write-up on Medium or your blog covering architecture decisions, failure modes, and eval results
Recorded agent trace (JSON + visualized graph) showing one full run end-to-end

publish: Post the Loom demo and repo link on LinkedIn and X tagging @LangChainAI, @AnthropicAI, and relevant SF AI builders; pin it to your profile for two weeks.
Submit a talk proposal to the next SF AI Engineer Summit, AI Tinkerers SF meetup, or a local LangChain/CrewAI community event.
Write a launch post on Hacker News (Show HN) framing it as 'How I built an enterprise research agent in X days' to capture technical credibility.
DM 5 SF-based AI engineering hiring managers at companies like Glean, Decagon, and Harvey with a 3-sentence pitch plus the demo link.
skills: Prompt engineering for reliability and reflection loops
System design for production AI systems
risks: Agent systems can be flaky and expensive in production — without a solid eval harness you will ship demos that break under load and quietly hemorrhage API budget.
The space is moving fast; a framework you learn today (LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen) may be obsolete in 6 months, so invest in the underlying patterns rather than the syntax.
Enterprise buyers care about security, latency, and audit trails more than clever prompts — a flashy demo without observability and guardrails will not survive a security review.
confidence: Very high — the signals are uniformly strong across GitHub activity, project potential, career value, and SF-specific enterprise demand, and the build project directly maps to roles being filled in the Bay Area right now.
